bg: The third book of the Pentateuch; so called in the Vulgate, after the LXX., because it treats chiefly of the Levitical service.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Law against sacrificing children to Moloch, Of children that curse their parents (vv. 1–9); Laws repeated, Holiness enjoined (vv. 10–27). People named: Molech, Moses.
ch.mh: Are we shocked at the unnatural cruelty of the ancient idolaters in sacrificing their children?
q: Read verses 1–9 (Law against sacrificing children to Moloch, Of children that curse their parents). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?

Where do you see the theme of family and generations in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Leviticus?

ch.mh: As these priests were types of Christ, so all ministers must be followers of him, that their example may teach others to imitate the Saviour.

ch.aq: Let us beware of hypocrisy, and examine ourselves concerning our sinful defilements, seeking to be purified from them in the blood of Christ, and by his sanctifying Spirit.

o: The feasts of the Lord, The Sabbath.
The Passover, The offering of first-fruits.
The feast of Trumpets, The day of atonement.

ch.mh: In this chapter we have the institution of holy times; many of which have been mentioned before.
q: Read verses 1–3 (The feasts of the Lord, The Sabbath). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 4–14 (The Passover, The offering of first-fruits), what do you learn about sacrifice and atonement?
Verse 3 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Leviticus 19:3. How do the two passages shed light on each other?

Where do you see the theme of holiness in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Leviticus?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: They were not to eat of their new corn, till God's part was offered to him out of it; and we must always begin with God: begin every day with him, begin every meal with him, begin every affair and business with him; seek first the kingdom of God.
ch.a: Memorize the key verse and come back to it each morning this week.

ch.aq: Let us watch against anger, do no evil, avoid all connexions with wicked people, and reverence that holy name which sinners blaspheme.

o: The sabbath of rest for the land in the seventh year.
The jubilee of the fiftieth year, Oppression forbidden.
Redemption of the land and houses.
bg: The third book of the Pentateuch; so called in the Vulgate, after the LXX., because it treats chiefly of the Levitical service.
Of Sin (the moon god), called also Horeb, the name of the mountain district which was reached by the Hebrews in the third month after the Exodus. Here they remained encamped for about a whole year.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The sabbath of rest for the land in the seventh year (vv. 1–7); The jubilee of the fiftieth year, Oppression forbidden (vv. 8–22); Redemption of the land and houses (vv. 23–34); Compassion towards the poor (vv. 35–38); Laws respecting bondmen, Oppression forbidden (vv. 39–55). People named: Moses. Places: Egypt, Sinai, Canaan.
ch.mh: All labour was to cease in the seventh year, as much as daily labour on the seventh day.
q: Read verses 1–7 (The sabbath of rest for the land in the seventh year). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 8–22 (The jubilee of the fiftieth year, Oppression forbidden), what do you learn about salvation and redemption?
Verse 10 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Jeremiah 34:8. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Moses’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of hope and restoration in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Leviticus?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: We cannot ransom our fellow-sinners, but we may point out Christ to them; while by his grace our lives may adorn his gospel, express our love, show our gratitude, and glorify his holy name.
ch.a: Thank God for His deliverance, and share what He has done for you with one person.

o: God promises to remember those that repent.
bg: The third book of the Pentateuch; so called in the Vulgate, after the LXX., because it treats chiefly of the Levitical service.
Of Sin (the moon god), called also Horeb, the name of the mountain district which was reached by the Hebrews in the third month after the Exodus. Here they remained encamped for about a whole year.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Promises upon keeping the precepts (vv. 1–13); Threatenings against disobedience (vv. 14–39); God promises to remember those that repent (vv. 40–46). People named: Jacob, Isaac, Abraham, Moses. Places: Egypt, Sinai.
ch.mh: This chapter contains a general enforcement of all the laws given by Moses; by promises of reward in case of obedience, on the one hand; and threatenings of punishment for disobedience, on the other.
q: Read verses 1–13 (Promises upon keeping the precepts). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 14–39 (Threatenings against disobedience), what do you learn about sin and repentance?
Verse 8 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Joshua 23:10. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Jacob’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of obedience in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Leviticus?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: God grant that we may, in this our day, consider the things which belong to our eternal peace.
ch.a: Ask God to search your heart, confess what He shows you, and make any right amends.

o: The law concerning vows, Of persons and animals.
Devoted things not to be redeemed.
bg: The third book of the Pentateuch; so called in the Vulgate, after the LXX., because it treats chiefly of the Levitical service.
Of Sin (the moon god), called also Horeb, the name of the mountain district which was reached by the Hebrews in the third month after the Exodus. Here they remained encamped for about a whole year.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The law concerning vows, Of persons and animals (vv. 1–13); Vows concerning houses and land (vv. 14–25); Devoted things not to be redeemed (vv. 26–33); Conclusion (vv. 34). People named: Moses. Places: Sinai.
ch.mh: Zeal for the service of God disposed the Israelites, on some occasions, to dedicate themselves or their children to the service of the Lord, in his house for life.

ch.aq: Having boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, let us draw near with a true heart, and in full assurance of faith, worshipping God with the more cheerfulness and humble confidence, still saying, BLESSED BE GOD FOR JESUS CHRIST.
ch.a: Thank God for His deliverance, and share what He has done for you with one person.
